title: Big Al McMordie Review 2026: Pricing, Record, Worth It?
description: Big Al McMordie review, checked 20 Nov 2026: BigAl.com prices from $30 picks to $2,395 a year, refund terms, his record claims checked, and buyer reports.
dek: Al McMordie has sold picks at BigAl.com since 1992 and now sells picks from 21 handicappers, from $30 a pick to $2,395 for a year. The site grades its own handicappers and posts daily results, and the outside boards we checked show him slightly profitable in 2026. There is no performance guarantee.

short_answer: Big Al's Sports Picks is a real, long running business. It names Al McMordie as the owner, lists a Los Angeles mailing address and a phone number he says he answers himself, publishes its prices and posts yesterday's results for every handicapper it sells, losses included.

Whether his picks make money over time is harder to answer. Most numbers on BigAl.com are graded by BigAl.com, and the career totals and awards on his page are seller claims with no full pick log we could open. The outside boards that also sell his picks show him slightly ahead: 733-629-20 and a 1.8% return for 2026 on SportsCapping, and 90-74 for +$932 in the 2025 NFL season on PickDawgz.

One useful check came out well. Between 7 and 20 Nov 2026 his career line on BigAl.com moved by 57 wins and 50 losses, and his SportsCapping 2026 line moved by exactly the same 57 wins and 50 losses, so the two sites appear to grade the same plays the same way.

Buyer feedback is old and mixed: a 2005 TheRX thread split between members who called the promotion misleading and members who said he answers his own phone and runs no boiler room, a 2012 Sportsbook Review post from a buyer who said a "Big Al" package lost $11,000, and seller chosen praise on BigAl.com. Treat Big Al as an established seller with a thin but real edge on outside boards, not a proven big winner. If you buy, buy short and log every pick yourself.

guarantee: BigAl.com does not sell a guarantee. The refund policy, effective 1 Jul 2020, says "There are no performance guarantees for any of the purchased picks or subscription packages" and "Refunds will not be provided due to poor predictive performance."

Single picks are refunded only in four cases: the game is suspended or cancelled, postponed more than four days, a baseball pitcher changes after the pick is posted, or the purchase was made after the game started. The policy says "none of these four exceptions apply to subscription purchases."

A second list is handled case by case and "may result in a credit for a future pick; partial refund, or substitution of handicapper": a handicapper posting no plays for a long stretch during a subscription, a big line move between release and purchase, or a handicapper's mistake. The FAQ also says that if a play is cancelled because the line moved, every buyer is refunded.

The FAQ offers something softer for losing runs. If a week or 30 day subscription fails to show a profit, graded at $1,000 a game, BigAl.com says it would "be happy to offer you a discount" on a new weekly or 30 day subscription. That is a discount on buying more, not money back, and it never covers what you lost on the bets themselves.

claims_note: How we checked: BigAl.com posts running totals but no full archive, so we compared its numbers on two dates and against outside boards. On 7 Nov 2026 the all sports line read 5332-4404; on 20 Nov it read 5389-4454, so the 107 picks in between went 57-50. On SportsCapping's 2026 board the same 13 days took him from 676-579 to 733-629, also 57-50. When two sites move by identical amounts, they are almost certainly grading the same plays the same way, which is a point in favour of the site's bookkeeping.

What the totals mean: 5389-4454 is 54.7%. If every play were a -110 bet, that would be a profit of about 490 units on roughly 10,800 units risked, a return near 4.5%. That is a good but modest edge, and it rests on lines at release from BetMGM, Caesars or DraftKings, whichever was best, so a buyer who bets later or at one book will usually do worse. The FAQ itself says shopping lines is worth about two percent.

The awards list is long, but almost every line is a rank in one sport over one window, such as "#1 NBA Playoffs Return on Risk." With many sports, many windows and several ranking categories, some first place finishes are likely for any active handicapper. The count has also grown: older bios still posted on VegasWinners say 45 championships, the current page says 72.

The "angle" and "system" records in pick titles, such as a "179-132 ATS NBA KNOCKOUT" or a "30-7 NHL SLAPSHOT CLUB" on 19 Nov 2026, describe how a past trend or run did, not his overall record. On that day he went 3-2 with those plays.
record: What a buyer can check outside BigAl.com: SportsCapping's 2026 season board (1 Jan to 20 Nov, flat $100 bets) listed "Big Al McMordie" 10th by profit at 733-629-20, 53.8% wins, $2,845 profit and a 1.8% return. PickDawgz' 2025 NFL table showed him at 90-74, 54.88%, +$932 on $100 bets. On 7 Nov 2026 SportsWatchMonitor's homepage showed small positive returns for 2023 to 2026, between 2.6% and 4.2% a year; that table was gone when we looked on 20 Nov. All of these sites also sell picks, and we could not open the full logs behind them, so they are third party numbers, not audits.

SportsHub, which tracks the free picks posted on BigAl.com, showed 6-8 and a -17.9% return on 14 graded free picks. That sample is far too small to mean anything, and free picks are not the paid plays.

What is the seller's own marketing: BigAl.com grades its handicappers itself, to win $1,000 a game, using the best line among BetMGM, Caesars and DraftKings at the time of the pick, according to its FAQ. It posts the previous day's results each morning at 3 am eastern (Al went 3-2, +$950 on 19 Nov 2026) and running totals on each handicapper page. We did not find a searchable archive of every past pick with its line and post time.

Contest results, such as the 2004 Stardust Invitational, would be independently verifiable if the organizers published them, but we did not find those records. We found no court or regulator action involving Al McMordie or BigAl.com in our searches.

our_data.text: Watchdog grades picks captured from public posts before the game starts. In this edition neither Al McMordie nor any BigAl.com handicapper is matched to a Watchdog graded record, so we make no claim about how these handicappers perform.
our_data.context: For scale: Al's page markets basketball seasons won in the mid 50s by win rate. On the Watchdog board on 20 Nov 2026, {{over60}} of {{established}} established accounts (100 or more graded picks) were at 60% or better, and the median established account won {{median_win}}% of its picks. At standard -110 odds a bettor needs about 52.4% to break even.

customers_intro: Independent customer evidence on Big Al is thin and mostly old. The testimonials on BigAl.com are chosen by the seller. The forum discussion we could open dates from 2004, 2005 and 2012, plus one 2025 Reddit post and a 2024 App Store review of a different site that mentions him. Reddit's archive full text search was failing on 20 Nov 2026, so the Reddit check relies on our saved library of earlier downloads. Below is everything we found and how much weight it can carry.

customers.text: We found eight independent posts on TheRX, Sportsbook Review, Reddit and the App Store, from 2004 to 2025, plus about ten testimonials the seller picked. The independent posts split. On the negative side, members of a 2005 TheRX thread said his ads overstated a disputed winner and that he sold computer trends, and a 2012 Sportsbook Review member said a "Big Al" big plays package cost them $11,000 at $1,000 a bet, though that post describes sales staff, which does not match how BigAl.com says it works. On the positive side, two TheRX members in 2005 said he answers his own phone and runs no boiler room, and a 2024 App Store reviewer unhappy with another pick site told readers to try Big Al instead. A 2004 TheRX member bought one $25 system play out of curiosity, and a 2025 Reddit user asked to share the cost of a month of his picks. Nobody posted a tracked long run record.

The homepage shows about ten testimonials, including podcast host Joe House and several clients who say they have used Al since the 1990s and praise his data driven approach and futures bets. One says Al had a losing NFL year before winning ones. These are selected and published by the seller.
A TheRX member posted one of Big Al's system plays, saying it cost $25 and that he seldom buys picks but was curious about an advertised 11-0 system. He did not report a result in what we could read.

On TheRX forum, a member objected to an ad that called a Golden State pick a cashed "Game of the Month" when, he said, the line sat at 2.5 or 3 for most of the day, and others mocked calling the next play a "BLOWOUT" winner. Another member wrote that his notes had the line at 3 for part of the day. This is a 21 year old dispute about one game.

In the same thread a member wrote that Al is "one of the best at selling plays" and gets carried away with hype, but that he does not run a boiler room, does not sell opposing plays, and answers his own phone. No results were posted.

Trustpilot showed no page for bigal.com on 7 Nov 2026, we found no Better Business Bureau profile we could confirm belongs to BigAl.com, and apart from the 2025 post below we found no Reddit thread discussing the service. Our library of Sportsbook Review, TheRX and Covers posts held no other buyer reports.

In the 2005 TheRX thread a member called Al a "BAD handicapper" and a scam, claiming buyers got little more than trends and systems from a computer program. He pointed to recent losses that, he said, the next promo did not mention.

Later in the same thread a member said he had bought plays from Big Al a few times and once talked with him on the phone at length. He said there was no staff of sales callers and no push toward a high roller package, though he disliked the promotion style and advised buyer beware.

A Sportsbook Review member wrote that a "Big al's big plays only package" left them down about $11,000 from November to late December, betting $1,000 a game, and that the sellers then pushed a doubled bet that also lost. They named two salesmen they dealt with by phone. The post does not name Al McMordie, and BigAl.com says callers speak only to Al, so this may concern a different "Big Al" service; we could not confirm which.
On Reddit, a user asked whether anyone paid for Big Al McMordie's picks and offered to split a month of them with someone. Our saved copy shows no buyer reply describing results.

In a one star App Store review of the SportsCapping app, a buyer unhappy with that marketplace's support told readers to look up Big Al instead. It is an endorsement in passing, with no detail about his results.

conflicts: BigAl.com sells picks from its whole roster and ranks the same handicappers in its own articles and leaderboards. A ranking published by the store that sells the picks is marketing, not an independent board.

The homepage promotes "Top Offshore Sportsbooks," and the sportsbooks page ranks offshore books with tracked links, including one at aff.betanysports.eu/big-al and one carrying the referral code ALMCMORDIE. Affiliate deals like these usually pay the site when readers sign up or lose. Offshore sportsbooks are not licensed by U.S. state regulators, so check the law where you live.

SportsWatchMonitor, SportsCapping, PickDawgz and PicksDepot, the outside sites that track or praise him, also sell handicapper picks, and SportsWatchMonitor sells his own packages. Most of the awards on his page come from monitor sites of this kind. None of them is a neutral auditor.
strengths: A named owner, a mailing address, a phone number with stated hours and a full price list.
Yesterday's results for every handicapper, losses included, are posted each morning, and the grading method is written down in the FAQ.
His BigAl.com totals and his SportsCapping record moved by the same 57-50 over the same 13 days, which suggests honest, consistent bookkeeping.
Outside boards show small profits for 2026 and the 2025 NFL season, more than most pick sellers can point to.
The refund policy is specific about when single picks are refunded, and free daily picks with written analysis let a reader see his style first.
concerns: No full public archive of every pick with line and post time. Career totals and awards are seller claims.
No performance guarantee and no refunds for losing picks. The FAQ offers only a discount on another subscription.
The margins are thin: 1.8% on SportsCapping for 2026. Worse lines or late buying could erase that for a customer.
The site carries offshore sportsbook affiliate links and referral codes.
Pick titles lean on hyped past trends such as "100% Perfect" angles, which say little about future results.
The same handicapper costs far more on SportsWatchMonitor ($999 for 30 days) than on BigAl.com ($395).
checklist: Ask for every pick from the last 12 months with the line, the odds and the time it was sent. A list of hot runs is not a record.
Compare his BigAl.com totals with an outside board such as SportsCapping before you pay, and use the lower number.
Count units, not wins. A 60% record at heavy favorites can still lose money, and his edge is a few percent.
Buy from the cheapest outlet. The same picks cost more on some monitor sites than on BigAl.com.
Write down each pick yourself the moment you receive it, with the line you can actually get, and shop at more than one legal book.
Give any handicapper a few hundred picks before you call them a winner. Short runs swing hard both ways.
faq: Yes in the sense that BigAl.com is a real, long running business with a named owner, an address, published prices and daily posted results. We could not verify his long term career record, because the site does not publish a full log of every pick.
How much does Big Al McMordie cost?

On 20 Nov 2026 his single picks were $30 each, and BigAl.com subscriptions ran from $100 for 7 days of baseball or hockey and $395 for 30 days of all sports up to $1,500 to $1,995 for a season and $2,395 for a year of all sports.
Does Big Al McMordie have a verified record?

Not a full one. BigAl.com grades its own picks, and outside boards that also sell picks showed him at 733-629-20 with a 1.8% return for 2026 and 90-74 in the 2025 NFL season. We could not open the logs behind these numbers, and Watchdog has no graded record for him.

Only in narrow cases. Single picks are refunded if the game is cancelled, postponed more than four days, already started, or a baseball pitcher changes. There are no refunds for losing picks; after a losing week or month the FAQ offers a discount on a new subscription.
Does Al McMordie really answer the phone?

That is what the FAQ says: callers speak directly to Al, not to salesmen, from 10 am to 4 am eastern. Two TheRX members in 2005 said the same. A 2012 Sportsbook Review complaint described sales staff at a "Big Al" service, but it did not name him and may concern a different seller.
Is Big Al McMordie worth it?

For the money you get daily picks with written analysis from a long time handicapper, with a $30 single pick as the cheapest entry. The outside numbers show a small edge, not a large one, so whether a buyer profits depends on getting lines as good as his at release, and there is no refund if the picks lose.
